questions.q: What does the Windows Git installer add alongside the git command itself?
options: A full Linux virtual machine
A built-in code editor that replaces VS Code
A GitHub account automatically
Git Bash, a Unix-style terminal most Git tutorials and this course assume
questions.explain: Git Bash gives Windows users a Unix-style terminal, matching the command examples used across most Git documentation.

questions.q: How do you confirm Git installed correctly, regardless of platform?
options: git --version
git --confirm
git status --check
There's no way to check — you just try a command and see
questions.explain: git --version prints the installed version, the same command on every platform.

questions.q: What does `git config --global user.name "..."` actually do?
options: It creates a new GitHub account with that name
It sets the name attached to every commit you make on this machine, across all repositories, until changed
It only applies to the current repository and must be repeated for every new project
It renames your computer
questions.explain: The --global flag means this identity setting applies machine-wide, which is why it's a one-time setup rather than a per-project step.

questions.q: Why does Git need your name and email configured before your first commit?
options: It doesn't — Git works fine with no identity set, ever
To send you marketing emails
Because that identity is what gets attached to every commit you make, recording who made each change
To verify your payment information
questions.explain: Every commit records an author, which is exactly what makes a commit history useful — knowing who changed what.

questions.q: Where does Git actually store the settings set with `--global`?
options: In a plain text file on your machine, such as ~/.gitconfig, editable directly in any text editor
In a remote database on GitHub's servers
Nowhere — global settings are not actually saved between sessions
Inside the repository's .git folder, so it must be set again for every project
questions.explain: Global Git config is just a plain text file on your machine, not a hidden database or per-project setting.
